identity.description: Book of Enoch documentary: Ethiopic and Dead Sea Scroll manuscripts, Romantic religious art, Mount Hermon, Qumran and Ethiopia as real evidence; painted reconstructions only for what no camera or painter ever captured.
identity.tone: reverent, mysterious, scholarly, grounded in evidence

ai_visual_prompt.style: real evidence first: ancient Ethiopic and Aramaic manuscripts, Dead Sea Scroll fragments, old printed Bibles, Romantic religious paintings and Gustave Doré engravings, Mount Hermon, the Qumran caves, Ethiopian monasteries. Only for scenes no camera or painter ever captured (the Watchers, the Nephilim, the house of crystal and fire, the abyss, the prison of the stars) use a reconstruction that looks like a lost 19th-century Romantic religious oil painting (dark chiaroscuro, storm light and firelight, muted umber, ochre and slate-blue palette, visible brushwork, fine craquelure, aged varnish) or a 19th-century Gustave Doré-style wood engraving (dense black-ink cross-hatching, aged cream paper); when a scene must feel photographic, a 35mm documentary film still with natural light, film grain, haze and muted colour. Dark, warm, desaturated documentary look throughout
ai_visual_prompt.composition: wide environmental framing; supernatural figures small, from behind, in silhouette or with faces in shadow; slightly off-centre; aged historical texture

artworks.query: William Blake Book of Enoch drawing
Gustave Doré fall of the rebel angels engraving

storytelling.narrative: Ancient text, then the evidence: what the Book of Enoch says, verse by verse, set against the manuscripts, the places and the history of its rediscovery.
storytelling.hook_strategy: Open on the oldest real manuscript evidence, then the claim
